```{r univariete - eloborate}
metric_names <- colnames(merged_df%>%
  select(-wsi,-fu_time,-progression,-flow,-pred,-dataset,))

univariate_results <- data_frame(var = as.character(),
                                 pval = as.numeric())

# merged_fu_eco <- left_join(merged_df_pred1,fu_times%>%select(wsi,fu_time), by = "wsi")
merged_fu_eco <- merged_df%>%
  filter(pred == 1)
for (var in metric_names) {
  cox_model <- coxph(as.formula(paste("Surv(fu_time, progression) ~", var)), data = merged_fu_eco)
  summary_model <- summary(cox_model)

  # Extract necessary statistics
  HR <- summary_model$coefficients[var, "exp(coef)"]
  se <- summary_model$coefficients[var, "se(coef)"]
  z <- qnorm(0.975) # z-value for 95% confidence interval

  # Calculate confidence intervals
  lower <- HR * exp(-z * se)
  upper <- HR * exp(z * se)

  summary_comdel_df <- data.frame(var = var,
                                  pval = summary_model$coefficients[var, "Pr(>|z|)"],
                                  HR = HR,
                                  lower = lower,
                                  upper = upper)

  univariate_results <- bind_rows(univariate_results, summary_comdel_df)
}

significant_vars <- univariate_results %>%
  filter(pval < 0.05)

# Print significant variables
print(significant_vars)
```

```{r}
metric_names <- colnames(merged_df%>%
  select(-wsi,-fu_time,-progression,-flow,-pred,-dataset,))

merged_fu_eco <- merged_df%>%
  filter(pred == 1)


multivariate_df_gen <- function(merged_fu_eco){
  # Step 1: Fit univariate models and extract those with p < 0.05
  significant_vars <- metric_names %>%
    keep(function(var) {
      model <- coxph(as.formula(paste0("Surv(fu_time, progression) ~ ", var)), data = merged_fu_eco)
      pval <- summary(model)$coefficients[1, "Pr(>|z|)"]
      !is.na(pval) && pval < 0.05
    })
  
  # Step 2: Build a model with only those variables
  formula_sig <- as.formula(paste("Surv(fu_time, progression) ~", paste(significant_vars, collapse = " + ")))
    cox_model_sig <- coxph(formula_sig, data = merged_fu_eco)
    
    # Extract detailed results for visualization
    coef_summary <- summary(cox_model_sig)$coefficients
    
    results_df <- data.frame(
      variable = rownames(coef_summary),
      coefficient = coef_summary[, "coef"],
      hr = exp(coef_summary[, "coef"]),
      se = coef_summary[, "se(coef)"],
      pvalue = coef_summary[, "Pr(>|z|)"],
      lower_ci = exp(coef_summary[, "coef"] - 1.96 * coef_summary[, "se(coef)"]),
      upper_ci = exp(coef_summary[, "coef"] + 1.96 * coef_summary[, "se(coef)"]),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ) %>%
      drop_na(hr)%>%
      mutate(
        # Create categories for visualization
        effect_direction = ifelse(hr > 1, "Increased Risk", "Decreased Risk"),
        effect_magnitude = case_when(
          abs(log(hr)) < log(1.5) ~ "Small",
          abs(log(hr)) < log(2) ~ "Moderate", 
          TRUE ~ "Large"
        ),
        pvalue = case_when(pvalue == 0 ~ .Machine$double.eps, 
                             TRUE ~ pvalue),
        significance = case_when(
          pvalue < 0.001 ~ "p < 0.001",
          pvalue < 0.01 ~ "p < 0.01",
          pvalue < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05",
          TRUE ~ "p >= 0.05"
        ),
        # Clean variable names for display
        clean_name = str_replace_all(variable, "_", " ") %>% 
                     str_to_title() 
                     # str_trunc(30)  # Truncate long names
      ) %>%
      arrange(pvalue)
}

results_df <- multivariate_df_gen(merged_fu_eco)
# results_df_discovery <- multivariate_df_gen(merged_fu_eco%>%filter(dataset == "MDA"))
```

```{r}
plot_forrest <- function(results_df, dataset = ""){
  top_n <- min(15, nrow(results_df))
  forest_plot_top <- results_df %>%
    # Fix 1: Use arrange() instead of sort(), and desc() for descending order
    arrange(desc(abs(log(hr)))) %>%
    # Fix 2: Use slice_head() instead of head() (more explicit)
    slice_head(n = top_n) %>%
    ggplot(aes(y = reorder(clean_name, -log10(pvalue)))) +
    geom_point(aes(x = hr, color = effect_direction, size = -log10(pvalue))) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci, color = effect_direction), 
                   height = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    # scale_x_log10()+#breaks = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4), limits = c(0.1, 10)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Increased Risk" = "#d32f2f", "Decreased Risk" = "#1976d2")) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.5, 2), name = "-log10(p)") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Top", top_n, "Features with Largest Effect Size",dataset),
      subtitle = paste("Multivariate Cox Regression (n =", nrow(merged_fu_eco), "samples)"),
      x = "Hazard Ratio (95% CI)",
      y = "Immune Response Features",
      color = "Effect Direction"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
  
  print(forest_plot_top)
  return(forest_plot_top)
}
```

```{r}
create_split_volcano <- function(results_df, break_point = 20) {
  
  results_df <- results_df %>%
    mutate(
      neg_log10_p = -log10(pvalue),
      y_adjusted = ifelse(neg_log10_p <= break_point, 
                         neg_log10_p,
                         break_point + (neg_log10_p - break_point) * 0.3) # Compress upper values
    )
  
  p2 <- results_df %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = coefficient, y = y_adjusted)) +
    geom_point(aes(color = effect_direction, size = abs(coefficient)), alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    # Add break indicator
    geom_hline(yintercept = break_point, linetype = "dotted", color = "orange", alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Increased Risk" = "#d32f2f", "Decreased Risk" = "#1976d2")) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 4), name = "Effect Size") +
    labs(
      title = "Volcano Plot with Compressed Y-axis",
      subtitle = paste("Values above -log10(p) =", break_point, "are compressed (dotted line)"),
      x = "Log Hazard Ratio (Coefficient)",
      y = "-log10(P-value) [compressed scale above break]",
      color = "Effect Direction"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    )
  
  return(p2)
}
```

```{r}
results_categorized <- results_df %>%
    mutate(
      category = case_when(
        str_detect(variable, "(?i)cd|immune|lymph|tcell|bcell") ~ "Immune Cells",
        str_detect(variable, "(?i)tumor|cancer|malig") ~ "Tumor Features",
        str_detect(variable, "(?i)stroma|fibro|collagen") ~ "Stromal Features",
        str_detect(variable, "(?i)vessel|vascul|endoth") ~ "Vascular Features",
        str_detect(variable, "(?i)inflam|cytok") ~ "Inflammation",
        str_detect(variable, "(?i)prolif|ki67|mitot") ~ "Proliferation",
        str_detect(variable, "(?i)apopt|necros") ~ "Cell Death",
        TRUE ~ "Other Features"
      )
    )
  
  # Create summary by category
  category_summary <- results_categorized %>%
    group_by(category, effect_direction) %>%
    summarise(
      count = n(),
      median_hr = median(hr),
      median_pvalue = median(pvalue),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = effect_direction, values_from = count, values_fill = 0) %>%
    mutate(
      total = `Increased Risk` + `Decreased Risk`,
      net_effect = `Increased Risk` - `Decreased Risk`
    )
  
  # Category barplot
  category_plot <- category_summary %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c("Increased Risk", "Decreased Risk"), 
                 names_to = "direction", values_to = "count") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = reorder(category, total), y = count, fill = direction)) +
    geom_col(position = "stack") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Increased Risk" = "#d32f2f", "Decreased Risk" = "#1976d2")) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(
      title = "Significant Features by Biological Category",
      x = "Feature Category",
      y = "Number of Significant Features",
      fill = "Effect Direction"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  print(category_plot)
```

```{r}
if (length(significant_vars) > 0) {
  formula_sig <- as.formula(paste("Surv(fu_time, progression) ~", 
                                  paste(significant_vars, collapse = " + ")))
  
  # Fit the multivariate model
  cox_model_sig <- coxph(formula_sig, data = merged_fu_eco)
  
  # Check for convergence issues
  if (cox_model_sig$iter >= cox_model_sig$control$iter.max) {
    warning("Model did not converge. Consider reducing variables or checking for collinearity.")
  }
  
  # Print model summary to check for extreme values
  print(summary(cox_model_sig))
  
  # Step 3: Create forest plot with error handling
  tryCatch({
    # Method 1: Basic forest plot
    fplot <- forest_model(cox_model_sig)
    print(fplot)
  }, error = function(e1) {
    message("Standard forest plot failed. Trying alternative approach...")
    
    tryCatch({
      # Method 2: Manual forest plot with controlled limits
      coef_summary <- summary(cox_model_sig)$coefficients
      hr <- exp(coef_summary[, "coef"])
      lower <- exp(coef_summary[, "coef"] - 1.96 * coef_summary[, "se(coef)"])
      upper <- exp(coef_summary[, "coef"] + 1.96 * coef_summary[, "se(coef)"])
      
      # Cap extreme values for plotting
      hr_capped <- pmax(pmin(hr, 100), 0.01)
      lower_capped <- pmax(pmin(lower, 100), 0.01)
      upper_capped <- pmax(pmin(upper, 100), 0.01)
      
      # Create data frame for plotting
      forest_data <- data.frame(
        variable = rownames(coef_summary),
        hr = hr_capped,
        lower = lower_capped,
        upper = upper_capped,
        pvalue = coef_summary[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
      )
      
      # Simple forest plot using base R
      library(ggplot2)
      fplot_manual <- ggplot(forest_data, aes(x = hr, y = factor(variable, levels = rev(variable)))) +
        geom_point(size = 3) +
        geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), height = 0.2) +
        geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
        scale_x_log10(limits = c(0.1, 10)) +
        labs(x = "Hazard Ratio (95% CI)", y = "Variables", 
             title = "Forest Plot - Cox Regression Results") +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
      
      print(fplot_manual)
      
    }, error = function(e2) {
      message("Alternative plotting also failed. Showing coefficients table instead:")
      
      # Method 3: Just print the results table
      coef_summary <- summary(cox_model_sig)$coefficients
      results_table <- data.frame(
        Variable = rownames(coef_summary),
        HR = round(exp(coef_summary[, "coef"]), 3),
        Lower_95 = round(exp(coef_summary[, "coef"] - 1.96 * coef_summary[, "se(coef)"]), 3),
        Upper_95 = round(exp(coef_summary[, "coef"] + 1.96 * coef_summary[, "se(coef)"]), 3),
        P_value = round(coef_summary[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 4)
      )
      
      print("Cox Regression Results:")
      print(results_table)
    })
  })
  
} else {
  message("No significant variables found after filtering")
}

# Additional diagnostic: Check for problematic variables
print("\nDiagnostic information:")
for (var in metric_names[1:min(5, length(metric_names))]) {
  var_data <- merged_fu_eco[[var]]
  if (is.numeric(var_data)) {
    cat(sprintf("Variable %s: Range [%.2e, %.2e], NA count: %d\n", 
                var, min(var_data, na.rm = TRUE), max(var_data, na.rm = TRUE), 
                sum(is.na(var_data))))
  }
}
```
